prompt: A PR for a new feature adds a custom `my_feature_icon.svg` because no existing icon was a perfect fit. As the reviewer, you:
choices: Approve — an optimized SVG under 1 KB adds negligible weight to the bundle
Ask to move the SVG into a shared theme folder so every platform can reuse it
Use or extend the Leo/Nala icon system and tag `@brave/nala-token-reviewers`
Ask them to inline the SVG markup in the component so no new asset file is added
explain: Leo is the canonical icon source on every platform. Bypassing it leads to inconsistency and duplicates, so flag it and tag `@brave/nala-token-reviewers`.

prompt: An Android feature needs a new icon. Where does it go?
choices: Add the icon entry to `android/nala/icons.gni`
Create `android/java/res/drawable/ic_my_new_icon.xml`
Add PNGs to each `drawable-*dpi` folder
Add it to the `leo_icons` list in `components/vector_icons/BUILD.gn`
explain: On Android, add icons to the Nala list in `android/nala/icons.gni` instead of creating new drawable resources.

prompt: A WebUI page needs an icon that isn't wired up yet. What's the right approach?
choices: Add `my_icon.svg` next to the page and reference it with ``
Base64-encode the SVG into a CSS `background-image` on a styled `<span>` wrapper
Add a new `.icon` file under `components/vector_icons/` and load it via a `chrome://resources` URL
List it in `leo_icons` in `ui/webui/resources/BUILD.gn`; render `<leo-icon name="my-icon-name">`
explain: For WebUI, add the icon name to the `leo_icons` array in `ui/webui/resources/BUILD.gn` and use `<leo-icon>`, not a raw `.svg` file.

prompt: A C++ Views toolbar button needs a new icon. How should it be added?
choices: Create `components/vector_icons/my_new_icon.icon` containing the vector path commands
Add `"my-icon-name"` to `leo_icons` in `components/vector_icons/BUILD.gn`
Add `"my-icon-name"` to `leo_icons` in `ui/webui/resources/BUILD.gn`
Rasterize it to PNG at 1x/2x and add it to the theme resources `.grd`
explain: For C++ browser UI, add the Leo icon name to `leo_icons` in `components/vector_icons/BUILD.gn` instead of creating a standalone `.icon` file.

prompt:
An Android PR adds this to `res/values/colors.xml`:

```xml
<color name="my_custom_blue">#1A73E8</color>
```

What should the reviewer say?
choices: Fine, but add a matching night-mode variant in `res/values-night/colors.xml` too
Rename it with a `brave_` prefix so it can't collide with upstream Chromium's color resource names
Use a Nala/Leo token like `@color/leo_color_button_background` and tag the Nala token reviewers
Move the hex value into a Java constant in `BraveColors` so it's defined in one place
explain: Don't define new Android color resources, because they bypass the design system and drift across themes and platforms. Reference an existing Nala/Leo token.

prompt: In a settings WebUI written in React, a teammate creates a `FancyCheckbox` component that wraps a styled `<input type="checkbox">`. Your review?
choices: Replace it with `Checkbox` from `@brave/leo/react/checkbox`
Fine, as long as its CSS uses Leo color variables
Fine, if they add the right `aria-*` attributes
Move `FancyCheckbox` to a shared components folder so others can reuse it
explain: In WebUI React, use Leo components instead of native HTML or hand-rolled equivalents. They're themed, accessible and design-approved. Tag `@brave/nala-token-reviewers` when flagging this.

prompt:
Convert this to follow the design system:

```tsx
<select value={value} onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}>
  <option value='a'>Option A</option>
  <option value='b'>Option B</option>
</select>
```
choices: Keep the native `<select>` and style it with Leo CSS variables so it matches the theme
`<Dropdown value={value} onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}>` keeping the `<option>` children
A Leo `<Button>` that toggles a custom popup list of options when clicked
`<Dropdown value={value} onChange={(e) => setValue(e.detail.value)}>` with `<leo-option>` children
explain: Use `Dropdown` from `@brave/leo/react/dropdown` instead of `<select>`. Its children are `<leo-option>` and its events carry the value in `e.detail.value`.

prompt:
A PR adds this component:

```tsx
function Spinner() {
  return <div className='spinner' aria-label='Loading...' />
}
```

What should the reviewer suggest?
choices: Fine — it has an `aria-label`, so it's accessible
Use `ProgressRing` from `@brave/leo/react/progressRing`
Use `Alert` from `@brave/leo/react/alert`
Move the spinner CSS into a shared stylesheet so other pages can reuse it
explain: Check whether Leo already provides a component before building one. For loading indicators, that's `ProgressRing`. Custom versions add maintenance and are usually less accessible.

Rename it to `kColorBraveSidebarPanelBackground` so Brave-specific IDs are easy to spot
Drop the intermediate ID; use `nala::kColorContainerBackground` directly at the call site
Move the mixer assignment into `side_panel_view.cc` so the color lives next to its only use
